heavyseas.opening.line1: April 1912. The Northern Star went down.
heavyseas.opening.line2: One boat got clear of her, overloaded, with water for a few days if it was fairly shared.
heavyseas.opening.line3: Nobody is coming that fast. You decide who lasts.
heavyseas.wake.jeweler.1: The jeweller woke with the case still under her arm and her hand on the clasp.
heavyseas.wake.jeweler.2: In the bow, the jeweller felt for the necklace under her collar before anything else.
heavyseas.wake.collector.1: The collector woke stiff with cold. He had not unbuttoned his greatcoat, and did not now.
heavyseas.wake.collector.2: The canvases were still rolled inside the collector's coat. One end of them was damp.
heavyseas.wake.captain.1: The captain counted heads before he counted anything else.
heavyseas.wake.captain.2: The captain woke in his uniform, cap and all. The money was still sewn into the lining.
heavyseas.wake.mate.1: The mate woke at the oars, his knuckles skinned from the rail.
heavyseas.wake.mate.2: The mate looked astern for his ship. There was only fog.
heavyseas.wake.hostess.1: The hostess still had the dipper in her lap.
heavyseas.wake.hostess.2: The hostess put up her hair, as though she were due behind the bar.
heavyseas.wake.sailor.1: The sailor woke wet through and wrung out his cuffs.
heavyseas.wake.sailor.2: The sailor looked once at the sky and said nothing.
heavyseas.wake.doctor.1: For twenty years, the doctor had let nobody else carry his bag.
heavyseas.wake.doctor.2: The doctor woke and took his own pulse before he looked at anyone else.
heavyseas.wake.kid.1: The child's hand rested on the tiller. Nobody had told him to hold it.
heavyseas.wake.kid.2: The child searched the faces aboard. His mother was not there.
